arxiv-1810-06695.title: Exploring the Use of Attention within an Neural Machine Translation Decoder States to Translate Idioms
arxiv-1810-06695.creator: Giancarlo D. Salton, Robert J. Ross, John D. Kelleher
arxiv-1810-06695.description: Abstract Idioms pose problems to almost all Machine Translation systems. This type of language is very frequent in day-to-day language use and cannot be simply ignored. The recent interest in memory augmented models in the field of Language Modelling has aided the systems to achieve good results by bridging long-distance dependencies.

arxiv-2011-10010.creator: Ilia Binder, Adi Glucksam, Cristobal Rojas, Michael Yampolsky

arxiv-2108-03981.title: A Credibility-aware Swarm-Federated Deep Learning Framework in Internet of Vehicles
arxiv-2108-03981.creator: Zhe Wang a , Xinhang Li a , Tianhao Wu ∗ a , Chen Xu a , Lin Zhang ba
arxiv-2108-03981.description: Abstract Federated Deep Learning (FDL) is helping to realize distributed machine learning in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). However, FDL’s global model needs multiple clients to upload learning model parameters, thus still existing unavoidable communication overhead and data privacy risks.

arxiv-2212-02337.title: Gaia - IGRINS synergy: Orbits of Newly Identified Milky Way Star Clusters
arxiv-2212-02337.creator: Elisa R. Garro, José G. Fernández-Trincado, Dante Minniti, Wisthon H. Moya, Tali Palma, Timothy C. Beers, Vinicius M. Placco, Beatriz Barbuy, Chris Sneden, Alan Alves-Brito, Bruno Dias, Melike Afşar, Heinz Frelijj, Richard R. Lane

The recent exquisite astrometric, photometric, and radial velocity measurements of the Gaia mission resulted in a substantial advancement for the determination of the orbits for old star clusters, including the oldest Milky Way globular clusters (MW GCs). Aims.

arxiv-2403-18972.title: Risk-Aware Robotics: Tail Risk Measures in Planning, Control, and Verification
arxiv-2403-18972.creator: Prithvi Akella*, Anushri Dixit*, Mohamadreza Ahmadi, Lars Lindemann, Margaret P. Chapman, George J. Pappas, Aaron D. Ames, and Joel W. Burdick
arxiv-2403-18972.description: Abstract Why is the consideration of risk integral to robotics? Consider the scenario of a rescue robot designed to navigate through a constrained environment to locate and rescue victims. Despite limited visibility and a ground that is potentially difficult to traverse, the robot is required to assess whether to execute a planned route or to seek an alternative route.

arxiv-2502-08814.title: Mortality simulations for insured and general populations
arxiv-2502-08814.creator: Asmik Nalmpatian, Christian Heumann
arxiv-2502-08814.description: Abstract This study presents a framework for high-resolution mortality simulations tailored to insured and general populations. Due to the scarcity of detailed demographic-specific mortality data, we leverage Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) and Monte Carlo simulations to generate refined mortality tables that incorporate age, gender, smoker status, and regional distributions.

arxiv-2505-12825.title: Theoretical Investigation on Inductive Bias of Isolation Forest
arxiv-2505-12825.creator: Qin-Cheng Zheng, Shao-Qun Zhang, Shen-Huan Lyu, Yuan Jiang, Zhi-Hua Zhou
arxiv-2505-12825.description: Abstract Isolation Forest (iForest) stands out as a widely-used unsupervised anomaly detector valued for its exceptional runtime efficiency and performance on large-scale tasks. Despite its widespread adoption, a theoretical foundation explaining iForest’s success remains unclear. This paper theoretically investigates the conditions and extent of iForest’s effectiveness by analyzing its inductive bias through the formulation of depth functions and growth processes.

arxiv-2508-13041.title: SPARQL in N3: SPARQL construct as a rule language for the Semantic Web (Extended Version)
arxiv-2508-13041.creator: Dörthe Arndt, William Van Woensel, Dominik Tomaszuk
arxiv-2508-13041.description: Abstract Reasoning in the Semantic Web (SW) commonly uses Description Logics (DL) via OWL2 DL ontologies, or SWRL for variables and Horn clauses. The Rule Interchange Format (RIF) offers more expressive rules but is defined outside RDF and rarely adopted. For querying, SPARQL is a well-established standard operating directly on RDF triples.

arxiv-2509-19705.title: Causal Machine Learning for Surgical Interventions
arxiv-2509-19705.creator: J. Ben Tamo, Nishant S. Chouhan, Micky C. Nnamdi, Yining Yuan, Shreya S. Chivilkar, Wenqi Shi, Steven W. Hwang, B. Randall Brenn, May D. Wang
arxiv-2509-19705.description: Abstract Surgical decision-making is complex and requires understanding causal relationships between patient characteristics, interventions, and outcomes. In high-stakes settings like spinal fusion or scoliosis correction, accurate estimation of individualized treatment effects (ITEs) remains limited due to the reliance on traditional statistical methods that struggle with complex, heterogeneous data.

arxiv-2509-20716.title: Episodic Feedback in Triple AGN Candidate SDSS J0849+1114 Revealed by Extended ionized gas Facilities: VLT:MUSE astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , EsoReflex ( Freudling et al. 2013 ) , PPXF ( Cappellari & Emsellem 2004 ) , DS9 ( Joye & Mandel 2003 ) , CLOUDY ( Chatzikos et al. 2023 ; Gu
arxiv-2509-20716.creator: Xiaoyu Xu (许啸宇), Meicun Hou, Zhiyuan Li, Sijia Peng, Zhao Su, Zongnan Li, Fuyan Bian, Junfeng Wang
arxiv-2509-20716.description: Abstract Galaxy mergers funnel gas toward the nuclei, igniting starbursts and active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The AGN feedback can reshape the host galaxy and regulate both star formation and super-massive black-hole (SMBH) accretion. Using VLT/MUSE integral-field spectroscopy, we conduct a spatially resolved study of the triple-AGN candidate SDSS J0849+1114.

arxiv-2511-07082.title: The Use of O 2 in Gas Mixtures for Drift Chambers
arxiv-2511-07082.creator: C. Voena
arxiv-2511-07082.description: Abstract The use of Oxygen in gas mixtures for drift chambers is highly discouraged because Oxygen, being strongly electronegative, is generally believed to lead, even in very small quantities, to extremely reduced drift electron attachment values, thus preventing the detector’s operation.

arxiv-2602-04354.title: Stellar Interpretation of Meteoritic Data and PLotting for Everyone (SIMPLE): Isotope Mixing Lines for Six Sets of Core-Collapse Supernova Models
arxiv-2602-04354.creator: Marco Pignatari, Mattias Ek, Georgy V. Makhatadze, Gábor G. Balázs, Lorenzo Roberti, James M. Ball, Borbála Cseh, Alessandro Chieffi, Chris Fryer, Falk Herwig, Chiara Incollingo, Thomas Lawson, Marco Limongi, Thomas Rauscher, Maria Schönbächler, Andre Sieverding, Reto Trappitsch, Maria Lugaro
arxiv-2602-04354.description: Abstract Bulk meteorites and their inclusions exhibit, for many chemical elements, isotopic variability produced by nucleosynthetic events in stars and supernovae before the formation of the Sun. While the exact astrophysical origins of these variations are still a matter of debate, their identification provides insights on the environment of the Sun’s birth and the formation of the Solar System.

arxiv-2602-13505.title: Constructing Quantum Convolutional Codes via Difference Triangle Sets Thanks: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. CCF-2145917.
arxiv-2602-13505.creator: Vahid Nourozi and David G. M. Mitchell
arxiv-2602-13505.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a construction of quantum convolutional codes (QCCs) based on difference triangle sets (DTSs). To construct QCCs, one must determine polynomial stabilizers X ⁡ ( D ) X(D) and Z ⁡ ( D ) Z(D) that commute (symplectic orthogonality), while keeping the stabilizers sparse and encoding memory small.

arxiv-2602-22181.title: Around homogeneity
arxiv-2602-22181.creator: Peter J. Cameron
arxiv-2602-22181.description: Abstract Forty-five years ago, a young researcher in finite permutation group theory encountered a paper by Robert Woodrow. The homogeneous triangle-free graph Woodrow described there seemed to be an infinite analogue of the Higman–Sims graph which had played an important role in the researcher’s thesis. The encounter changed the course of the researcher’s career.

europmc-pmc6868369.title: Tandem repeats lead to sequence assembly errors and impose multi-level challenges for genome and protein databases.
europmc-pmc6868369.creator: Tørresen OK, Star B, Mier P, Andrade-Navarro MA, Bateman A, Jarnot P, Gruca A, Grynberg M, Kajava AV, Promponas VJ, Anisimova M, Jakobsen KS, Linke D.
europmc-pmc6868369.description: The widespread occurrence of repetitive stretches of DNA in genomes of organisms across the tree of life imposes fundamental challenges for sequencing, genome assembly, and automated annotation of genes and proteins. This multi-level problem can lead to errors in genome and...

pmc-10545934.title: Structure preserving adversarial generation of labeled training samples for single-cell segmentation
pmc-10545934.creator: Ervin Tasnadi, Alex Sliz-Nagy, Peter Horvath
pmc-10545934.description: SummaryWe introduce a generative data augmentation strategy to improve the accuracy of instance segmentation of microscopy data for complex tissue structures. Our pipeline uses regular and conditional generative adversarial networks (GANs) for image-to-image translation to construct synthetic microscopy images along with their corresponding masks to simulate the distribution and shape of the objects and their appearance.

pmc-11351187.title: Validation of an Instrument for Detecting Problematic Internet Use in Adolescents
pmc-11351187.creator: Mateo Pérez-Wiesner, Kora-Mareen Bühler, Jose Antonio López-Moreno, Laura Piccardi, Emanuela Mari, Alessandro Quaglieri
pmc-11351187.description: Problematic internet use (PIU) has drawn attention due to its potentially negative consequences on individuals’ social and personal lives. At present, a consensus on diagnostic criteria for problematic internet use remains elusive, leaving uncertainty regarding its classification as a distinct mental disorder. Extensive research efforts are underway to investigate its underlying causes, risk factors, and correlated adverse consequences.

pmc-11557280.title: Engaging communities in therapeutics clinical research during pandemics: Experiences and lessons from the ACTIV COVID-19 therapeutics research initiative
pmc-11557280.creator: David A Wohl, Stacey J Adam, Kevin W Gibbs, Ari L Moskowitz, Thomas L Ortel, Upinder Singh, Nikolaus Jilg, Teresa H Evering, William A Fischer, Babafemi O Taiwo, Eric S Daar, Christopher J Lindsell, Susanna Naggie, Russell L Rothman, Sarah E Dunsmore, M Patricia McAdams, Julia Vail, Dushyantha Jayaw
pmc-11557280.description: This manuscript addresses a critical topic: navigating complexities of conducting clinical trials during a pandemic. Central to this discussion is engaging communities to ensure diverse participation. The manuscript elucidates deliberate strategies employed to recruit minority communities with poor social drivers of health for participation in COVID-19 trials.

pmc-11668265.title: Synergistic Effects of Anti-echinococcosis Drug Candidates Combined With Atovaquone in Culture Assays and Mice With Primary Infections of Echinococcus multilocularis
pmc-11668265.creator: Hirokazu Kouguchi, Masahito Hidaka, Hiroyuki Matsuyama, Naoki Hayashi, Tomohito Koyano, Ryo Nakao, Nariaki Nonaka, Kinpei Yagi, Shigehiro Enkai
pmc-11668265.description: BackgroundAlveolar echinococcosis (AE) is a fatal zoonotic disease distributed mainly in the Northern Hemisphere. At present, its curative treatment relies on surgery, and the development of effective drugs is needed. We previously demonstrated the anti-echinococcal effect of atovaquone (ATV) as a mitochondrial complex III inhibitor in both in vitro and in vivo experiments.

pmc-12836836.title: Long-term straw incorporation improves nutrient accumulation in wheat seedlings by changing the soil’s hydrothermal environment to promote root growth
pmc-12836836.creator: Hongmei Cai, Feifei Wang, Weixiang Huang, Li Yang, Mengmeng Zhang, Jiyuan Zhang, Baoqiang Zheng, Shan Jiang, Jincai Li, Xiang Chen
pmc-12836836.description: Crop straw incorporation plays an important role in improving soil environment, increasing crop yields and developing green and sustainable agriculture. However, the effects of long-term straw return on soil’s hydrothermal environment and the growth of wheat seedlings have not been well explored.

pmc-13019513.title: Abdominal Leak Point Pressures During Cough and Valsalva: What Do the Different Maneuvers Hide?
pmc-13019513.creator: Carolina Veiga e Moura, Ana Lopes, Bercina Candoso
pmc-13019513.description: This study analyzes abdominal leak point pressures (ALPP) during Valsalva and cough maneuvers in patients with stress urinary incontinence (SUI) (pure or mixed), with the aim of clarifying the different psychopathological mechanisms of urethral incontinence behind leakage with each.This is a retrospective study of women with stress or mixed incontinence submitted to urodynamic testing with ALPP in 2024.

pmc-13308284.title: Ecological Reassembly of the Milk Microbiome and Its Associated Resistome During the Dry Period in Dairy Cows
pmc-13308284.creator: Lan Ma, Jing Qu, Xiubo Li, Yiming Liu
pmc-13308284.description: Simple SummaryUnderstanding how the mammary microbial community changes across the dry period and early lactation is important for improving udder health and reducing unnecessary antibiotic use in dairy cows. In this study, milk samples were collected at three key stages: before dry-off, immediately after calving, and one month postpartum.
